projects.title: Formula SAE Chassis Rules Check
projects.summary: Checked the Formula SAE chassis model against Section F.6 of the 2026 rules: 24 items, 22 passed, 1 not applicable, 1 failed.
details: Measured tube sizes, triangulation and member positions directly in the SolidWorks model.

F6.4.4 failed: the upper side impact member sits slightly outside the allowed zone (it must fit within 290 mm and 375 mm). I noted that it needs to shift at least 0.75 mm and left the dimensions and notes for the chassis team lead.
F6.4.5 passes but needs a ride height check that the lower side impact tube is at least 75 mm off the ground.

projects.title: Water Filter Design
projects.summary: Team-built water filter that raised transmittance from 9.0% to 20.5% while cutting filtration time from 6:40 to 3:00 across three designs.
details: Goal: produce low-turbidity water using simple, limited materials. Success meant a high spectrometer transmittance reading with a short filtration time.
Data showed sand was the most influential material and the drainage rock had little effect, so we kept the sand, reduced the other materials and rearranged the layers.
Final design alternated sand and pea gravel layers over a cotton round, which kept the cotton from clogging and nearly doubled transmittance (10.5% to 20.5%).
Next step: add more gravel at the bottom and compact it to reduce clogging.

projects.title: Balsa Wood Tower
projects.summary: Team-built tower under 15.0 g that held 122.5 lbs, more than three times the 40 lb minimum. It weighed 14.67 g.
details: Challenge: placing sticks of different masses where they carry the most force.
Solution: after researching with my team, we put the heaviest sticks on the edges, where the force is greatest, and built mounting so the cross members could distribute force more efficiently.
